endorsements.quote: Crucially, the output is formulated to link each claim back to specific sources: the text includes inline citations or reference IDs corresponding to the original documents.
The system maintains an immutable audit log capturing the full decision process.
Next, an AI reasoning module (built on a RAG architecture) processes the retrieved texts together with the patient data to generate a recommendation.
The knowledge base is not static; it is updated continuously as new evidence emerges.
Provenance and evidence grading: Every content item is tagged with comprehensive provenance metadata, including authors, publication dates, and source types.

unlisted_practices: Use a secondary critic agent to verify that a generated recommendation is supported by the cited text before display to the clinician.
Use ensemble retrieval combining multiple search algorithms such as semantic search and BM25 in RAG systems.
Assign relevance scores to retrieved passages and use only those above a high-certainty threshold in reasoning.
Use terminology services such as SNOMED-CT and UMLS to map clinical queries to normalized concepts before retrieval.
Store audit log entries in a tamper-evident permissioned distributed ledger with hashed entries and off-chain storage of clinical data.
Use progressive disclosure in the user interface, presenting concise recommendations with primary citations and expandable detail.
Screen knowledge base sources for demographic representativeness and flag or warn clinicians when evidence has demographic gaps.
Display evidence grading such as GRADE levels alongside AI recommendations.

screen.reason: This paper presents a conceptual architecture/framework combining RAG, provenance metadata, and audit logging for trustworthy clinical AI, without presenting empirical validation.
